coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > applies a.description: applies a percentage discount to the cart total
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > applies a.reason: The assertion only checks that result is defined, not that the discount was applied. A broken implementation that returns the cart without discounting (or returns any defined value) would pass this test. The test lacks any assertion on the actual value or structure of the result to verify the discount was calculated correctly.
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > applies a.weakestAssertion: expect(result).toBeDefined() - checks only existence, not correctness. Should also verify result.total equals 90 (100 - 10%)
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > applies a.suggestedMutation: function applyCoupon(cart, coupon) { return cart; } - returns cart unchanged without applying discount, yet assertion passes

coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > refuses to.description: Stacking two coupons is refused: the second call leaves the cart total exactly as the first coupon left it, and reports STACKING.
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > refuses to.reason: The three assertions together verify all aspects of the described behavior: (1) the second coupon application returns an error via `expect(second.ok).toBe(false)`, (2) the error is specifically "STACKING" via `expect(second.error).toBe("STACKING")`, and (3) the cart total remains unchanged from the first coupon's result via `expect(cart.total).toBe(90)`. If the implementation allowed stacking, returned a different error, or modified the total on the second call, at least one assertion would fail. The test would also fail if the first coupon didn't work correctly, since the expected total of 90 would not be reached.
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > refuses to.weakestAssertion: The assertion `expect(second.ok).toBe(false)` only checks that an error occurred, not which error. However, this weakness is covered by the companion assertion `expect(second.error).toBe("STACKING")`, which specifically verifies the error type.
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > refuses to.suggestedMutation: Modify the implementation to apply both coupons together (e.g., return `ok: true` and set `cart.total = 72` instead of rejecting with `ok: false`). This would violate the description by allowing stacking, and the test would fail on both the `second.ok` and `cart.total` assertions.

coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > rejects an.reason: The three assertions comprehensively verify the described behavior. The test would fail if an expired coupon were applied to the cart, if the function returned success instead of failure, or if it returned the wrong error code. These cover the realistic ways the rejection behavior could break.
coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > rejects an.weakestAssertion: expect(result.ok).toBe(false) is the most foundational assertion—if this passes but result.error is wrong, assertion 2 catches it; if this passes but cart.total changes, assertion 3 catches it.

coupon.test.ts::applyCoupon > works corr.reason: The description "works correctly" is too vague to be falsifiable. A reader cannot determine what specific behavior is being tested, what the expected outcome should be, or what observable result would prove the implementation broken, without seeing the test body itself.

coupon.test.ts::checkout > when the paym.reason: The test only asserts that the charge function was called with the correct argument. It makes no assertions about order creation—there is no check that an order was not created, no assertion about the checkout return value, and no verification that order-creation code was skipped. If the implementation broke and created an order despite payment decline, this test would still pass.
coupon.test.ts::checkout > when the paym.weakestAssertion: expect(charge).toHaveBeenCalledWith(100) only verifies the payment processor mock's arguments, not whether an order was created.
coupon.test.ts::checkout > when the paym.suggestedMutation: Modify checkout() to create and return an order even when charge.declined is true. The test would still pass because it never checks the checkout result or asserts that order creation was prevented.
